info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package leaderboard is the ranking of who uses AI most, in your org and globally.

post.summary: Records a verified bug report or bounty PR award on the leaderboard, opts the recipient's handle into public listing, and sends a celebratory email announcing their points, AI credits, and updated leaderboard rank.
post.description:
Records a verified bug report or bounty PR award on the leaderboard,
opts the recipient's handle into public listing, and sends a celebratory email
announcing their points, AI credits, and updated leaderboard rank. SuperAdmin only.

post.summary: Seeds the derived usage rollup from ledger history — the rows written before the incremental view existed, which that view can never capture.
post.description:
Seeds the derived usage rollup from ledger history — the rows written
before the incremental view existed, which that view can never capture. SuperAdmin
only. Because the rollup accumulates, a second unguarded run would double every
day it re-reads, so it refuses with 409 when the rollup already holds rows unless
force=true is passed; forcing WILL double-count.

get.summary: Ranks AI usage over a window, either the users of the caller's own org or organizations against each other, and always reports the caller's own standing even when it falls outside the returned page.
get.description:
Ranks AI usage over a window, either the users of the caller's own org
or organizations against each other, and always reports the caller's own standing
even when it falls outside the returned page. Identities are private by default: a
caller sees themselves, plus the peers or orgs that opted into public listing, and
only an admin sees their own org's members named. Cross-org spend is restricted to
platform admins. When the warehouse is not connected the board answers empty with
available=false rather than a fabricated rank.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description:
Scope picks the board: "personal" (default) ranks the caller among their own
org's users, "org" is that same org board named for an admin, "global" ranks
organizations against each other.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Metric is the value ranked: tokens (default), requests, or cost.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Period is the window ranked: day, week, month (default) or all.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps the rows returned, clamped to 100. Defaults to 10, which is also
what a non-positive or unparseable value takes.

get.summary: Returns the per-day usage series for ONE authorized subject — the points a contribution heatmap and a timeline are drawn from, gap-filled so every day in the range is present.
get.description:
Returns the per-day usage series for ONE authorized subject — the points a
contribution heatmap and a timeline are drawn from, gap-filled so every day in the
range is present. Authorization is resolved server-side from the validated
principal, so a caller can never widen the subject past what they are entitled to:
a non-admin reads only themselves and their own org. subject=project answers empty
with a note, because the usage ledger records no project column yet. When the
warehouse is not connected the series answers empty with available=false rather
than fabricated days.

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: Subject is what the series is about: "user" (default), "org" or "project".

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:
ID names the subject within what the caller is entitled to see. Omitted (or
"me") it is the caller themselves, or their own org. Another user requires org
admin and must belong to the caller's org; another org requires a SuperAdmin.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: From is the first day of the range, "2006-01-02". Defaults to 90 days back.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description:
To is the last day of the range, "2006-01-02". Defaults to today; the span is
clamped to 366 days.

get.summary: The README badge of a listed org's leaderboard rank, as an SVG
get.description: Public once the org opts into the public leaderboard (PUT /v1/leaderboard/optin or PUT /v1/leaderboard/optin/org). Name the handle or org slug with the .svg extension. theme=dark|light, style=flat|card, fields= and label= (at most 24 characters) choose the look. Cached hourly in-process and at the edge (stale-while-revalidate 24h) and answers 304 to a matching ETag; every word on it is escaped. An unlisted org and an unknown handle are the same 404. No credential is needed.

get.summary: Ranks everyone on the hanzo.ai/beta waitlist by one score: 1 per star on GitHub verified for the record and 1 per founder link followed, plus 1 per org that signed up with its referral code, plus 20 per such org that has made metered spend, plus 1 per 100,000 tokens the person used, all time.
get.description:
Ranks everyone on the hanzo.ai/beta waitlist by one score: 1 per star
on GitHub verified for the record and 1 per founder link followed, plus 1 per org
that signed up with its referral code, plus 20 per such org that has made metered
spend, plus 1 per 100,000 tokens the person used, all time. Ties go to the earlier
application. Share clicks count for nothing.

Everyone who ever applied is on it. A form filed before the person had an
account is a row of its own (no name, score 0, the day it was filed) until their
account's record claims it, and the record then begins when the form did.

A row is named only for a person who opted into the public board (PUT
/v1/leaderboard/optin); the caller always sees their own row named. Tokens are a
range on every row and exact on a named row and the caller's. `tokens` and
`referrals` say whether the warehouse and the referral service answered; a
term that did not is left out of every score alike.

A named handler, not a closure, so zipdoc can lift this prose into the registry.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit caps the rows, clamped to 1..100. Defaults to 25, which is also what a
non-positive value takes.

get.summary: Returns the ranked bug hunters and bounty contributors, and the recent bug and bounty awards.
get.description: Returns the ranked bug hunters and bounty contributors, and the recent bug and bounty awards.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit caps the hunter and award rows returned, clamped to 1..100. Defaults to 25.

get.summary: Stream the board's live lines to anyone as Server-Sent Events
get.description: Holds one text/event-stream open and pushes a `message` frame for each line as it happens, after replaying the last 20. `data` is `{id, kind, at, handle, detail}`, where kind is joined, referred, tried, milestone, hour, bounty, level or expert. `handle` is masked in the middle, whole for an org that listed itself and empty for one that withdrew. At most 30 lines a minute. A `: ping` comment is written every 25 seconds. There is no resume: a reader that reconnects is replayed the last 20. No credential is needed to read it.

get.summary: Returns every ranked org as a star, for a page to draw the community as a galaxy: each star holds its band in the reward program's level table, a coarse size (a factor of two), the star of the org that referred it, if any, and, only for the ranks the reader has earned a view of, its exact points and the name the standing shows for it.
get.description:
Returns every ranked org as a star, for a page to draw the community as a galaxy: each
star holds its band in the reward program's level table, a coarse size (a factor of
two), the star of the org that referred it, if any, and, only for the ranks the reader
has earned a view of, its exact points and the name the standing shows for it. The
window is the standing's: a signed-in reader sees their own star, five ranks below it
and as many above as their points have earned; a reader who is not signed in sees the
last ranks, where a newcomer starts. Every other star has `points` of -1 and no name,
and is still drawn. The stars are columns of equal length, best first, and `center` is
the tokens used and the orgs active in the last 24 hours. A star's id is opaque: it is
the same wherever this answer mentions that star, names no org, and is replaced on the
next read, about a minute later. A signed-in reader gets `self`, the id of their own
star. Names are the standing's: masked in the middle, whole where the org listed
itself, empty where it withdrew. No org id, handle or email is sent. No credential is
needed to read it.

get.summary: Returns the caller's own public-listing preference and their org's, each with whether the caller may change it.
get.description:
Returns the caller's own public-listing preference and their org's,
each with whether the caller may change it. Public listing is opt-in and private
by default, so a fresh caller reads listed=false for both.

put.summary: Sets the CALLER's own public-listing preference on the leaderboard.
put.description:
Sets the CALLER's own public-listing preference on the leaderboard.
Self only: the row written is keyed by the caller's validated ledger identity, so
this can never edit another member's visibility whatever the request says. A
caller opting in with no handle is given their username, so a listed row never
renders as "Anonymous" to its own owner.

put.summary: Sets the ORG's listing on the cross-org global board.
put.description:
Sets the ORG's listing on the cross-org global board. Only an admin of
the caller's own org — an org admin or a platform SuperAdmin — may change it, and
the org written is the caller's validated tenant, never a value from the request.
Listing consents to publishing the org's usage VOLUME; cross-org spend stays
restricted to platform admins regardless.

get.summary: Returns how fast the platform is being used and is spreading, as counts by day for thirty days and by hour for the last day: tokens used, orgs active, orgs signed up, orgs that came through a referral link, orgs using a model for the first time (with the models most tried), and how many different models were in use (variety).
get.description:
Returns how fast the platform is being used and is spreading, as counts by day for
thirty days and by hour for the last day: tokens used, orgs active, orgs signed up,
orgs that came through a referral link, orgs using a model for the first time (with
the models most tried), and how many different models were in use (variety). Every
series is read from where cloud records it; one that cannot be read is left out and
named in `missing`, and the ones nothing records today (orgs trying a product,
shares) are always named there. Counts only: no org, no name. No credential is
needed to read it.

get.summary: Returns the public board of who has used and built the most on Hanzo, shown as a window around the reader.
get.description:
Returns the public board of who has used and built the most on Hanzo, shown as a
window around the reader. Every org IAM holds is ranked, by points: tokens used,
referrals, verified stars, follows and bounty awards. A signed-in reader sees their own rank, the ranks
just below it and as many above it as their points have earned; the rest are
counted in `locked` and never sent. A reader who is not signed in sees the last
ranks, where a newcomer starts. Names are masked in the middle; the reader's own is
whole, an org that listed itself is whole, and one that withdrew has none. No
credential is needed to read it.

costCents.description:
CostCents is the day's spend in whole US cents. A series is only ever returned
for a subject the caller is authorized to see, so this is never withheld: 0 means
no spend that day.

day.description: Day is the UTC calendar day this point covers, "2006-01-02".

requests.description:
Requests is the subject's request count on this day. 0 is a real, quiet day: the
series is gap-filled, so every day in the range is present whether or not
anything happened.

tokens.description:
Tokens is prompt+completion tokens on this day — normally the heatmap's
intensity, scaled against ActivityTotals.MaxTokens.

activeDays.description:
ActiveDays counts the days with any usage at all — the streak/consistency number.
Compare it against len(days) for the share of days the subject showed up.

costCents.description: CostCents is the window's spend in whole US cents, the sum of Days[].CostCents.

maxRequests.description:
MaxRequests is the same ceiling for a request-based heatmap — the busiest single
day's request count, 0 for an idle window.

maxTokens.description:
MaxTokens is the busiest single day's token count: the ceiling to normalize a
token heatmap against, so the darkest cell is that day. 0 for an idle window,
which a client must not divide by.

requests.description: Requests is the sum of Days[].Requests over the whole window.

tokens.description: Tokens is the sum of Days[].Tokens over the whole window.

available.description:
Available is false when nothing could be read: the warehouse is not connected,
the rollup is not ready, or the subject is one the ledger cannot attribute (see
Note). Days is then empty because there is no answer, not because there was no
activity.

days.description:
Days is the gap-filled series, one point per calendar day from From up to (not
including) To, in ascending order, zero-valued days included. Always a list,
never null.

from.description: From is the first day in Days, "2006-01-02" inclusive.

id.description:
ID is the subject the server actually read, after resolving "me"/empty to the
caller and bounding it to what they may see — a ledger "owner/name" for a user,
an org id for an org. Echoed so a client can confirm whose series it holds.

note.description:
Note explains an empty-but-not-broken answer in plain words — today only
subject=project, which the usage ledger records no column for. Present only when
there is something to say; show it instead of an empty chart.

source.description:
Source names the table the series was aggregated from (the derived daily rollup,
hanzo.usage_rollup_daily).

subject.description: Subject echoes what the series is about: user|org|project.

to.description:
To is the EXCLUSIVE upper bound, "2006-01-02" — the day AFTER the last point in
Days. A request for to=2026-03-31 answers to=2026-04-01 with 2026-03-31 last.

totals.description:
Totals are the window's sums plus the busiest-day ceilings a heatmap scales
against. Derived from Days — nothing here is read separately.

of.description:
Of is how many people are on the waitlist: every account that applied, and
every lead that applied before it had an account.

referrals.description:
Referrals is whether referrals were counted; false when the referral service
did not answer, and no record's score has them then.

rows.description: Rows are the top of the waitlist, best first.

tokens.description:
Tokens is whether token usage was counted; false when the warehouse did not
answer, and no record's score has it then.

you.description:
You is the caller's own row wherever it ranks; null when the caller holds
no record.

applied.description:
Applied is the day the application began, 2006-01-02: the record's own, or the
day of the lead it claims when that was earlier.

name.description:
Name is the handle its owner listed under on the public board; null for a
person who did not opt in, whom the page calls a builder. The caller's own
row is always named.

qualified.description: Qualified is how many of them have made metered spend.

rank.description: Rank is the record's place, 1 first.

referrals.description: Referrals is how many orgs signed up with the record's referral code.

score.description:
Score is what the row is ranked by: points, referrals, qualified referrals
and tokens, as GET /v1/leaderboard/beta's description states.

tokens.description:
Tokens is the person's all-time token usage as a range: 0, <1M, 1M-10M,
10M-100M, 100M-1B or 1B+.

tokensUsed.description:
TokensUsed is the exact count, on a named row and the caller's; absent on
every other.

you.description: You marks the caller's own row.

creditsCents.description: CreditsCents records the AI credits (in US cents) granted alongside this award.

email.description: Email is the recipient's email address to send the celebratory reward + rank update notification to.

handle.description: Handle is the display name shown on the bounty board.

id.description: ID is an optional idempotency key for the award; generated when empty.

org.description: Org is the recipient's organization slug.

points.description: Points overrides the default points for Kind when positive.

summary.description: Summary is a one-line description of the bug report or fix.

target.description: Target names the repo, PR, or issue (e.g. hanzo-inc/cloud#123).

user.description: User is the recipient's IAM username within Org.

award.description: Award is the recorded bounty award.

emailSent.description: EmailSent is true when a celebratory notification email was dispatched to Email.

hunter.description: Hunter is the recipient's updated standing on the bounty board.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the unix timestamp (seconds) when the award was recorded.

creditsCents.description: CreditsCents is the AI credit grant in US cents awarded with this bounty.

handle.description: Handle is the recipient's display name.

id.description: ID is the unique award identifier.

points.description: Points is the leaderboard points awarded.

summary.description: Summary describes what was reported or fixed.

target.description: Target is the repository or issue reference (e.g. hanzo-inc/cloud#index-lock).

hunters.description: Hunters are the top-ranked bug hunters and bounty contributors, best first.

recentAwards.description: RecentAwards are the newest verified bug reports and bounty payouts.

self.description: Self is the signed-in caller's own bounty standing when signed in.

badge.description: Badge is the gamified tier title earned by the contributor.

bountiesMerged.description: BountiesMerged is how many bounty pull requests this contributor has landed.

bountyPoints.description: BountyPoints is the sum of points earned from bug reports and bounties.

bugsReported.description: BugsReported is how many verified bug reports this contributor has filed.

creditsEarnedCents.description: CreditsEarnedCents is the total AI credits in US cents granted for bounties and bug reports.

globalTokenRank.description: GlobalTokenRank is the contributor's global organization rank by token volume (0 if unranked).

handle.description: Handle is the contributor's public display handle.

org.description: Org is the contributor's organization slug when listed.

rank.description: Rank is the contributor's 1-based standing on the bounty board.

self.description: Self marks the signed-in caller's own row.

tokensUsed.description: TokensUsed is the contributor's all-time token volume in the warehouse.

totalScore.description: TotalScore is the org's points by client.Points, the one score every board shares.

activeOrgs24h.description: ActiveOrgs24h is how many different orgs used any of them.

tokens24h.description:
Tokens24h is the tokens used in the last 24 hours: the sum of the pulse's tokens
by hour.

band.description: Band is each star's index in the response's bands.

id.description: ID is each star's opaque id, of no use after the next read.

mask.description:
Mask is the name the standing shows for the org where the reader's reveal window
holds it: masked in the middle, whole where it listed itself, empty where it
withdrew. It is empty for every star outside the window, which has points of -1.

points.description:
Points is each star's exact score where the reader's reveal window holds it, and
-1 where it does not: a star the reader has not earned a view of.

size.description:
Size is each star's coarse size, from 0: the bit length of its points, a factor of
two. It is every star's, in or out of the window, and is what a sky is drawn from.

sponsor.description: Sponsor is the id of the star that referred this one; empty where none did.

available.description:
Available is false when the warehouse is not connected or a source could not be
read and none ever was: the stars are then empty because nothing could be read.

bands.description:
Bands are the band names of the reward program's level table, lowest first; a
star's band indexes them.

center.description: Center is what the platform did in the last day.

self.description:
Self is the id of the signed-in reader's own star; empty for a reader who is not
signed in or whose org the board does not hold.

anonymous.description:
Anonymous is true when this subject's identity was withheld and Handle is the
"Anonymous" placeholder: the metric is real, the name is not. Render it as an
unnamed row, never as someone actually called Anonymous.

costCents.description:
CostCents is this subject's spend in whole US cents (not dollars, not
millicents). It is 0 unless the viewer is entitled to this subject's spend —
their own row, an admin looking at their own org, an explicitly cost-ranked
board, or a platform admin on the global board — so 0 means "withheld or zero",
and the two are deliberately indistinguishable.

handle.description:
Handle is the display identity to render: the peer's chosen handle if they opted
into public listing, their username if the viewer is an admin of their org, the
org's chosen display name (or its id) on an org board, and the literal
"Anonymous" when the identity is withheld. Never an email or a raw ledger id.

metric.description:
Metric is the value the board was ranked by, copied from Requests, Tokens or
CostCents according to the request's metric. It is what a client sizes bars
against without having to know which metric was asked for.

rank.description:
Rank is this subject's 1-based standing in the window, 1 being the top. Rows are
ordered by the ranked metric descending (ties broken by request count), and a
board is always the top of the list — there is no offset paging — so the first
row is always rank 1 and rank is also the row's index + 1.

requests.description:
Requests is how many AI requests this subject made in the window. Volume is not
sensitive, so it is reported for every row including anonymized ones.

self.description:
Self marks the caller's own row so a client can highlight it in place. At most
one row carries it, and it is never set on an org board — org rows carry no user
identity, so the caller's own org standing arrives in LeaderboardView.Self.

tokens.description:
Tokens is prompt+completion tokens this subject spent in the window. Like
Requests it is reported for every row.

available.description:
Available is false when the usage warehouse is not connected or its rollup is not
ready. Rows is then empty because nothing could be read — not because nobody used
anything. Show that difference; never render an unavailable board as a real one.

end.description:
End is the EXCLUSIVE upper bound of the window, "2006-01-02" — the day after the
last one counted. A board through today reports tomorrow's date here.

metric.description: Metric echoes the value ranked: tokens|requests|cost.

period.description:
Period is the window's canonical label: day|week|month|all. The server resolves
aliases (7d, 30d, today, …) to these, so this may differ from what was sent.

rows.description:
Rows are the ranked subjects, best first, at most the requested limit of them.
Always a list, never null: an empty one means nothing was read, not an error.

scope.description: Scope echoes the board that was served: personal|org|global.

self.description:
Self is the caller's own standing, reported even when they fall outside Rows.
Absent when the caller's ledger identity cannot be resolved, or when the query
behind it failed — never faked to keep the shape tidy.

source.description:
Source names the table these numbers were aggregated from (the derived daily
rollup, hanzo.usage_rollup_daily), so an operator can tell exactly what was read.

start.description:
Start is the first day counted, "2006-01-02" inclusive. Empty for period=all,
which has no lower bound at all.

subject.description:
Subject is what the rows stand for — "user" on a personal or org board, "org" on
the global one. It tells a client whether Handle names a person or a company.

total.description:
Total is how many subjects were ranked in the window — the org's active users, or
the active/opted-in orgs on the global board. It is the universe the ranks are
out of, so it is normally larger than len(rows).

days.description: Days is one count a day, aligned with PulseView.Days.

hours.description:
Hours is one count an hour, aligned with PulseView.Hours. Absent for a series
recorded by the day alone.

count.description: Count is how many orgs used it for the first time in the window.

available.description: Available is false when no series could be read at all.

days.description: Days are the thirty days counted, oldest first, "2006-01-02" in UTC, ending today.

hours.description: Hours are the twenty-four hours counted, oldest first, RFC 3339 in UTC, ending in the current hour.

missing.description:
Missing names every series not drawn: the ones nothing records (products,
shares) and the ones whose source could not be read just now.

models.description: Models is the orgs that used a model for the first time, by day.

orgs.description: Orgs is the orgs that used anything.

referred.description: Referred is the orgs that signed up through a referral link.

signups.description: Signups is the orgs that signed up.

tries.description: Tries is the models orgs used for the first time in the window, most first.

variety.description:
Variety is how many distinct Hanzo models were asked for, platform wide, in each
day and each hour (the ledger's model column; "models" above is the first tries).
An id is compared lower-cased and trimmed, so "Zen4" and "zen4 " are one model; the
empty id and any id with a "/" in it, the vendor's path for the model served, do
not count. Two different ids for one model are two here: no alias table is read.

costCents.description:
CostCents is the caller's own spend in whole US cents. Always populated — your
own spend is never withheld from you — so here 0 really does mean zero.

handle.description:
Handle is how the caller appears on this board: their chosen handle, falling back
to their username, on a user board; their org id on the global board. Present
even when unlisted — this is the caller looking at themselves.

listed.description:
Listed says whether the caller is publicly visible on this board: opted in on a
user board, org opted in (or the viewer is a platform admin) on the global one.
False is the prompt to offer the opt-in, and explains an unranked global self.

metric.description:
Metric is whichever of the three values above the board was ranked by, so a
client can compare the caller against the rows without re-reading the request.
Metric <= 0 is exactly the case that leaves Ranked false.

ofTotal.description:
OfTotal is the size of the universe Rank is out of — "rank N of OfTotal". On a
user board that is the org's users with any usage in the window; on the global
board it is every active org for a platform admin, and the count of opted-in
orgs for everyone else.

rank.description:
Rank is the caller's 1-based standing, computed as (subjects whose windowed
metric strictly exceeds the caller's) + 1. It is exact against the whole ranked
universe, not just the returned page, so it can far exceed len(rows). Read it
only when Ranked.

ranked.description:
Ranked is false when the caller holds no position: they had no usage in the
window, or (on the global board) their org has not opted into public listing and
so is not ranked against a set it never joined. Rank is then 0 and means nothing.

requests.description: Requests is the caller's own request count in the window, 0 if they were idle.

tokens.description: Tokens is the caller's own prompt+completion tokens in the window.

at.description: At is the points at which it unlocks.

more.description: More is At minus the reader's points: what is left to earn.

reveal.description: Reveal is how many more ranks above the reader that rung unlocks.

handle.description:
Handle is the name to show: masked, or full for the reader's own row and for an
org that listed. Empty for an org that withdrew; show it as "A builder".

points.description: Points is the score the board ranks by.

rank.description: Rank is the 1-based place on the whole board, not the window.

self.description: Self marks the reader's own row.

handle.description: Handle is the reader's own full handle.

next.description: Next is the next rung to unlock; absent when nothing above is locked.

rank.description: Rank is the reader's place on the whole board.

ranked.description:
Ranked is false for a reader with no usage and no award yet. Rank is then 0 and
the window is the one a newcomer sees.

available.description:
Available is false when the warehouse is not connected: Rows is then empty
because nothing could be read, not because nobody has used anything.

locked.description:
Locked is how many ranks lie above the first row, which the reader has not
earned a view of. They are counted, never sent.

rows.description: Rows are the ranks the reader may see, best first. Always a list.

scored.description: Scored is how many of them hold any point; the rest are at the bottom.

self.description: Self is the reader's own place; absent when not signed in.

total.description: Total is how many orgs are ranked: every org IAM holds that is not a held one.

before.description:
Before bounds the seed to ledger rows written before this RFC3339 instant.
Defaults to now, and is snapped down to UTC midnight — the rollup's grain, so
the seeded days and the guarded days are the same set. Pass the day the
incremental view started capturing, so seed and view never share a day.

force.description:
Force must be exactly "true" to seed a rollup that already holds rows. It is
spelled as a string, not a flag, because the guard has always compared this
value literally — "1" and "yes" do NOT force.

forced.description: Forced is true when the caller overrode the already-populated guard.

seededBefore.description: SeededBefore is the RFC3339 upper bound the seed actually used.

status.description: Status is "ok" — a seed that did not run answered an error instead.

org.description:
Org is the caller's org's listing preference on the cross-org board, and whether
this caller is allowed to change it. It is read for every caller — a member sees
where their org stands even though only an admin may edit it.

user.description: User is the caller's OWN listing preference, and whether they may change it.

display.description:
Display is the name shown for the org on that board: 1-40 characters of
letters, digits, space, dot, underscore, apostrophe or hyphen. Left empty on a
listing opt-in it defaults to the org id.

listed.description:
Listed publishes the org on the cross-org global board when true, and withdraws
it when false.

canManage.description:
CanManage is true only for an admin of this org (or a platform SuperAdmin) — the
callers whose write of the org preference will be accepted.

display.description:
Display is the name shown for the org on that board. Empty when none was chosen;
opting in without one defaults it to the org id.

listed.description:
Listed is true when the org has opted onto the cross-org global board. False —
the default — keeps the org off it entirely; the org's own members still see
their own board. Listing consents to publishing usage VOLUME, never spend.

handle.description:
Handle is the display name shown on a listed row: 1-40 characters of letters,
digits, space, dot, underscore, apostrophe or hyphen. Left empty on a listing
opt-in it defaults to the caller's username.

listed.description:
Listed publishes the caller's row to other viewers of the board when true, and
anonymizes it when false.

canSet.description:
CanSet is false when the caller's ledger identity cannot be resolved (no user
name on the principal). Writing the preference would fail, so hide the control.

handle.description:
Handle is the display name on the caller's listed row. Empty when they never
chose one; opting in without a handle sets it to their username, so a listed row
is never blank.

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
